source.snippet: Microsoft Intune manages Android Enterprise personally-owned work profiles. Identity/productivity is Google Workspace on a managed Google domain, federated to Microsoft Entra (OIDC SSO). Goal: users use native Google Drive/Gmail in the work profile, signed in with their Workspace account. Symptom: the Workspace account can be added to the work profile but sign-in completes via the Entra redirect and then native Google apps still prompt for re-authentication or fail silently in the work profile. Environment involves domain allow-lists, OIDC federation, and Android Enterprise policy conflicts between two competing MDM philosophies.

problem_statement: IT admins running hybrid Microsoft Intune + Google Workspace environments on Android Enterprise cannot reliably get native Google apps (Drive, Gmail) to authenticate properly inside Intune-managed work profiles when identity is federated via Entra OIDC — resulting in silent failures and broken MDM enforcement.
target_segment: IT administrators and enterprise mobility engineers at mid-market companies using both Microsoft Intune and Google Workspace.
notes: Single post but represents a real enterprise IT environment (company with both Microsoft and Google stacks — a very common hybrid setup). Buyer context is clear: this is a sysadmin at a company spending time on a configuration failure. A diagnostic guide, tested configuration template, or managed integration service could command consulting fees or a SaaS subscription. Signal is weak (1 post) but the underlying problem is well-known in the MDM space.
